story.title: Bringing Safe Water Closer to Every Family
dis: In Barmer and Jaisalmer, women and children can walk up to three kilometres each day to collect water. The water is not always safe to drink, and the time spent fetching it can mean missed school, fewer work hours and repeated stomach illnesses.

We install deep-bore hand pumps close to where families live and fit each site with a filtration unit. Before a source is used, water quality is checked and the site is mapped so the community can understand where its water comes from.

Each pump is supported by a trained village committee. Members learn basic maintenance, keep a simple service log and collect a small monthly contribution for spare parts and repairs. This helps the water point remain useful long after installation.
We track each village from site assessment to installation and follow-up testing. Progress updates are shared here so supporters can see what has been completed and what still needs attention.

faqs.question: What if a pump breaks down?
faqs.answer: Each village committee is trained and keeps a spare-parts fund. For larger faults, our field team visits within a week.

faqs.question: Can I follow my gift?
faqs.answer: Yes. Milestones and updates on this page are refreshed as each village is completed.

faqs.question: What happens if we raise more than the goal?
faqs.answer: Extra funds go to the next set of villages in the same district, or to maintenance, and we will say so in an update.

school-for-every-child.location: Rural districts of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh

story.title: Helping Every Child Stay in School
dis: Many children leave school not because they lack curiosity, but because their families cannot always afford uniforms, books, shoes or daily meals. These basic needs can become barriers to attendance and learning.

This programme works with local schools to identify children who are most at risk of dropping out. Support is directed toward practical essentials that help children arrive at school prepared and ready to participate.
Alongside learning kits, the programme is expanding meal support with partner schools. Teachers and school teams help monitor attendance and identify when a child may need additional support.
Attendance and delivery milestones are reviewed each term. We share progress updates so families, schools and supporters can understand what has been delivered and where further help is needed.

milestones.title: Partner schools signed up
milestones.description: 18 schools agreed to share attendance data and identify children at risk.

milestones.title: First term kits delivered
milestones.description: Books, uniforms and shoes reached 700 children.

milestones.title: Meal programme in all schools
milestones.description: Daily meals are being rolled out school by school.

milestones.title: Year-end attendance review
milestones.description: Results published for every partner school.

faqs.question: How are children chosen?
faqs.answer: Schools identify children most at risk of leaving, using attendance and family circumstances.

faqs.question: Is the money used for anything else?
faqs.answer: No. Gifts to this cause fund only the items in the breakdown above.

health-camps-on-wheels.location: Remote blocks of Odisha and Jharkhand

story.title: Taking Essential Healthcare to Remote Communities
dis: For families in remote parts of Odisha and Jharkhand, reaching the nearest hospital can take hours. As a result, routine check-ups may be delayed and manageable health problems can become more serious.
Mobile clinics bring basic healthcare closer to villages on a planned route. Each visit can include a nurse, basic diagnostic equipment and a supply of essential medicines for common health needs.

When a patient needs treatment beyond the clinic’s capacity, the team provides a referral to an appropriate nearby health facility and follows up where possible. Clear routes and visit schedules help communities know when care will be available.
Clinic activity is monitored through village visits, patient counts and service updates. These records help the team identify communities that need more regular access and plan future visits.

milestones.title: Clinic 1 and 2 on the road
milestones.description: Two vehicles fitted out and covering 40 villages.

milestones.title: Third clinic launched
milestones.description: Vehicle fitted, staff hired and routes planned.

milestones.title: All 60 villages on schedule
milestones.description: Every village gets a visit every two weeks.

faqs.question: Is care free for patients?
faqs.answer: Yes. Check-ups and the medicines we carry are free at the clinic.

faqs.question: What about serious cases?
faqs.answer: We refer the patient to the nearest hospital and follow up to check they received care.

skills-for-steady-incomes.location: Peri-urban areas around Lucknow and Kanpur

story.title: Building Skills for More Reliable Incomes
dis: Many women and young people have the motivation to earn an income but lack access to practical training, tools or the small amount of starting capital needed to begin.

Participants take a short, hands-on training course and choose a trade that fits their interests and local demand, such as tailoring, repairs or food preparation. Training is designed to help participants build useful skills they can apply in everyday work.

After training, eligible participants receive a starter kit and a small grant to help them begin working. A mentor checks in over the following six months to discuss progress, challenges and next steps.

The programme tracks enrolment, training completion and the transition into trading or paid work. Income reviews help the team understand which types of support are working and where participants need additional guidance.

milestones.title: First cohort of 60 enrolled
milestones.description: Training has started in two centres.

milestones.title: Income review
milestones.description: We measure income change six months after launch and publish the results.

faqs.question: Is the grant a loan?
faqs.answer: No. It is a one-time grant, and participants do not repay it.

faqs.question: How do you measure success?
faqs.answer: We compare household income before the programme and six months after it.

rebuild-village-libraries.location: Villages across Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh

story.title: Reopening Village Libraries and Growing a Love of Reading
dis: A welcoming library can give children a quiet place to read, learn and imagine new possibilities. In some villages, however, library buildings have leaking roofs, empty shelves or have remained closed for years.

Volunteers and local carpenters help repair buildings, restore shelves and organise age-appropriate books in Hindi and English. The work focuses on making each space safe, useful and inviting for children and families.

Local reading groups are involved from the beginning and help manage opening hours, lending and activities. Community ownership makes it easier for each library to stay active after the initial repairs are complete.

Progress is tracked through library reopenings, book collections and the establishment of local reading groups. Future updates will share completed repairs and the next locations scheduled for support.

milestones.title: First 4 libraries reopened
milestones.description: Repairs done, shelves built and books in place.

milestones.title: Libraries 5 to 8
milestones.description: Roof repairs and shelving under way.

milestones.title: Final 4 libraries
milestones.description: Repairs, books and reading group set-up.

faqs.question: Who looks after the library afterwards?
faqs.answer: A local reading group, trained by us, manages opening hours and lending.

faqs.question: Can I donate books instead of money?
faqs.answer: Book donations are welcome through our team, so we can match titles to what each library needs.

Clean-water-for-villages.location: Villages across Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh

story.title: Creating Sustainable Access to Clean Village Water
dis: Reliable access to safe water supports health, education and daily life. In villages where water sources are distant or unreliable, families may spend hours collecting water and still have concerns about its quality.

This initiative aims to improve local access by assessing village needs, identifying suitable water points and planning installations with community members. Water quality checks help guide decisions about filtration and ongoing use.

Community participation is central to long-term maintenance. Local representatives can help monitor water points, report faults and coordinate repairs so that infrastructure continues to serve households.
Progress updates should document the villages assessed, water points installed, test results and maintenance arrangements. This makes the work easier for residents and supporters to follow.

milestones.title: Village water needs assessed
milestones.description: Priority villages and suitable water points are identified with community input.

milestones.title: Water points installed and tested
milestones.description: Installations are checked and water quality results are recorded before regular use.

milestones.title: Community maintenance groups trained
milestones.description: Local groups receive guidance on routine checks, reporting faults and arranging repairs.

faqs.question: How are villages selected?
faqs.answer: Priority is based on local water access needs, source suitability and consultation with community representatives.

faqs.question: How do you check water quality?
faqs.answer: Water is tested as part of the site assessment and follow-up process. Results and next steps should be included in project updates.

faqs.question: Who maintains the water point?
faqs.answer: Community representatives are involved in monitoring and reporting issues, with maintenance arrangements planned for each site.

faqs.question: How can I follow progress?
faqs.answer: Check the milestones and updates on this page for information about assessments, installations, testing and community training.
